title: committed_calls keeps the newest call rows by git grep path order, which is not strictly chronological
goal: bl_intake.committed_calls keeps the newest REPEAT_ROWS_MAX call.tool rows by their ts, whatever order git grep reads the ops sidecars in (a late-written sidecar holding old-week rows no longer evicts the rows of the latest closed ISO week), returns them oldest first, and counts the rows it left out as before

run:
import sys, tempfile, subprocess, pathlib, json
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_intake as b
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
o = pathlib.Path(d, b.STORE_REL, "ops"); o.mkdir(parents=True)
def row(ts, cls): return json.dumps({"event": "call.tool", "ts": ts, "class": cls}) + "\n"
(o / "a.jsonl").write_text(row("2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", "new") + row("2026-10-02T00:00:00Z", "new2"))
(o / "b.jsonl").write_text(row("2026-09-01T00:00:00Z", "old"))
def g(*a): return subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com", *a], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
g("init", "-q"); g("add", "."); g("commit", "-qm", "x")
rows, over = b.committed_calls(d, budget=2)
print(rows, over)
sys.exit(0 if [k for _, k in rows] == ["new", "new2"] and over == 1 else 1)
